w1  ECOM1 · 6760 documents

Brain — shared files and workspaces for agents collaborating on BitGN challenges

Session s8320 is this task's separate working copy. Use brain_run(session="s8320", seq=1, source=...). Copy next_seq for each new run; retry uncertain calls with the same seq. The SDK examples below are Python source for brain_run.

Choose a workspace from the index and load the documents your task needs. First contact with a workspace supplies its shared AGENTS.md; read it before making changes. Put s8320 before every command.

Operate through Python programs on the server; brain is already bound to this session:

  brain s8320 run 'print(brain.tree("wID"))'
  brain s8320 run 'print(brain.search("wID", "a phrase"))'
  brain s8320 run 'print(brain.outline("dID1", "dID2"))'

Consider the outlines, then read selected sections in another run:

  brain s8320 run 'print(brain.read("dID", section="Current status"))'

search() returns a compact text page: at most 10 documents and 4,000 bytes,
one short excerpt each, and an exact next-page expression. Follow it as needed,
then outline selected handles. Use search_matches() for structured data in loops.
outline() shows heading trees with line intervals and byte sizes, including
nested sections. Select by heading title or starting line: section=12.
Small files can be read whole with read("dID"). Printed output has a 24,000-byte
budget per run.

Use returned workspace/document handles; wID/dID/dID1/dID2 are placeholders.
Read, think, then run another snippet. Reads include your draft edits.
If a run encounters new instructions and attempts writes, its writes roll back;
read the instructions and send it again.

Python SDK — common calls (content is str, bytes or an input handle; refs also accept wID:path):
  brain.workspaces(); brain.workspace(wID); brain.tree(wID, path="")
  brain.files(wID, path="", prefix="", glob=None)
  brain.search(wID, text, path="", prefix="", glob=None, limit=10)
  brain.outline(*refs); brain.read(dID, section=None); brain.read_bytes(dID); brain.stat(dID)
  brain.create(wID, path, content); brain.write(dID, content); brain.edit(dID, old, new)
  brain.input(name); brain.export(ref, name="file", revision=None)
  brain.move(dID, path); brain.delete(dID); brain.restore(dID); brain.exists(ref)
  brain.status(); brain.diff(ref=None); brain.history(ref); brain.undo()
  brain.commit(summary=None); brain.discard()
  brain.refresh(); brain.conflict(ref); brain.resolve(dID, content="reconciled text")
  brain.create_workspace(name); brain.rename_workspace(wID, name)
  brain.sandbox.submit(dID, revision=REV, trials=1); brain.sandbox.queue()
  brain.sandbox.status(job); brain.sandbox.result(job); brain.sandbox.trace(job)
Sandbox jobs start after commit. Read brain.help("sandbox") and brain.sandbox.sdk().
Progress slides (/progress): in a new task, brain.slides.publish(dID, revision=REV), then
brain.commit(). Read brain.help("slides") for the folder-backed deck contract.

files/search: path= selects a file/subtree; prefix= matches a literal path prefix.
glob= matches the full workspace-relative path; * spans directories.
Example: brain.files(wID, path="04_projects", glob="*ai-native*") finds nested files.
Path utilities: brain.path.join(path, *parts), dirname(path), basename(path),
normpath(path), relpath(path, start="."), split(path), splitext(path), isabs(path).
All path helpers are under brain.path; no import needed. Details: print(brain.help("path")).
brain.artifacts — immutable HTML snapshots. Publish captures exact bytes; commit activates the URL. Edit the source and publish again for a new edition. Revoke withdraws one workspace publication. The server must have --web-public-url configured. Published HTML has scripts, forms, frames and external resources disabled.
More signatures and workspace verbs: print(brain.help()) or print(brain.help("METHOD")).
Named files: run --input NAME=FILE supplies brain.input(NAME); --output NAME=FILE
saves brain.export(ref,name=NAME). Bytes travel separately from printed output.
Guidance: brain.help("reading"), "editing", "artifacts", "recovery", "runtime", "transfers". Diagnostics: brain.doctor().
Use print() to return results. Each invocation has fresh Python variables;
document edits persist. All writes in a successful run form one undo step.
An uncaught error rolls back that run's writes.

Review: brain s8320 run 'print(brain.diff())'
Finish: brain s8320 run 'brain.commit()' or brain s8320 run 'brain.discard()'
Commit publishes all changes atomically. Commit/discard closes this session
only if the whole run succeeds.
Lost response: brain s8320 run --retry.
